contract: Shutdown closes admission and resolves only when no active attempt and no scheduled retry can later start. Retry timers are request work, not unrelated maintenance timers. Cancelling a timer removes it from the owned pending set. Shutdown does not require successful completion of cancelled requests.

evidenceRequirements.description: Explain how the supplied guard preserves its contract across relevant ownership/time boundaries. Do not require knowledge of an unseen sibling. Evaluator counterfactual only: A failed attempt schedules a retry at time10 and leaves active count zero. Shutdown sees no active work and resolves. The pending timer fires after resolution and starts another attempt unless closed admission is checked/cancelled. A drain over both active and owned timers plus cancellation prevents post-drain admission.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: Normal retry before shutdown remains allowed; shutdown with an active attempt waits for settlement; repeated shutdown is idempotent; a timer already dequeued before close is still rejected by the admission gate.

forbiddenClaims: Production outage, real data exfiltration or universal safety without supplied evidence.
A missing contract establishes either a definite defect or unconditional protection.
Simulated time or offline passing tests establish real scheduler/OS behavior or model improvement.
independence: non-independent, same-workflow authorship and public artifacts
